scenarios.title: Review an AI troubleshooting claim
scenarios.summary: Check a generated diagnosis and a traffic forecast against independent observations before making a network change.
scenarios.objective: Run an independent incident probe and review the generated cause against the observed carrier and policy. Collect the supplied later reading and evaluate the forecast against the alert threshold. Apply the repair supported by the evidence and verify that the other exchanges keep their required outcomes.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare the actual observation with the stated requirement, then retry the affected step.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A generative system can propose an explanation in everyday language. A precise-looking explanation can still be wrong. Use a fresh observation that could prove it wrong, such as a probe of the claimed carrier failure.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: A predictive system estimates a later value from previous observations and other inputs. Machine learning can learn patterns in earlier traffic, for example to recognize unusual usage. Compare the forecast and later reading to the same alert threshold. One correct comparison says little about accuracy on other traffic.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: If the carrier works and the installed policy lacks a required rule, verify the desired rule before publishing. Check that the intended exchange works and that an excluded service remains excluded. A high load estimate alone cannot justify changing a route.

scenarios.explanation: The independent source determines whether the proposal matches this incident. The later reading tests the alert prediction. Applying the approved rule recovers the affected exchange and preserves both control cases.
hints: A returned carrier probe rules out the specific carrier failure described in a claim.
Compare forecast and observed value with the threshold, using the same boundary for each.
Read the desired and installed policy first. Publish only when the supplied evidence supports it.
scenarios.simplifications: Supplied fictional model outputs, historical and later usage samples, and actual bounded virtual path observations. No AI inference, model training, hosted AI, external telemetry or device change occurs.

scenarios.title: Review a declarative device change
scenarios.summary: Repair a desired configuration plan so it changes only the approved resources, then confirm that a second preview is empty.
scenarios.objective: Restore the declared recovery profile to the desired document. Retire only the supplied obsolete profile. Apply the approved plan while keeping the unrelated port’s binding and the excluded paths. Confirm both permitted paths and preview again so the current document has no unapplied changes.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare the actual observation with the stated requirement, then retry the affected step.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A desired configuration describes how resources should look. A plan compares it with the current state and proposes changes. Review what would be created, updated or removed before applying.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: Terraform plans tell you what resource changes are proposed. Ansible check mode can show what supported tasks expect to change, and diff mode can show before and after values. Some modules have limited check support. This lab uses an offline comparison over its own supplied document.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: A valid document can propose deletion of a valuable resource. Compare the removal with the work order and restore missing records. After applying the approved changes, preview again. An empty plan for the same document indicates that the two states match in this lab.

scenarios.explanation: The desired document keeps the recovery profile, changes the approved bindings and retires the obsolete item. The second preview detects any mismatch with the applied configuration, while the virtual Ethernet trials verify the work order.
hints: The list of planned removals comes from comparing with the applied configuration.
Keep the exact value of the recovery profile, including its description. An unused profile can still be necessary for a future recovery.
After an edit, preview before applying. Preview once more after applying and use Check workspace to verify actual paths.
scenarios.simplifications: Fixed source-bound port profiles and bindings, typed JSON and actual virtual Ethernet checks. No Ansible or Terraform parser, module, provider, task execution, real device, credentials, deployment, or remote state is used.
